newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower after setting new high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower after setting new high.

text.p: Swiss shares ended slightly lower in volatile trade, ending a four-day record run after the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) set an all-time intraday high of 5,611 points, the first time it has broken above 5,600.
The SMI ended down 11.7 points, or 0.21 percent, at 5,576.1.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 4.62 points, or 0.13 percent, to end at 3,525.48.
Bourse volume totaled 2.94 billion Swiss francs.
An early recovery on Wall Street after Monday's slide boded well for the Swiss bourse, one trader said.
But trade was nervous, with one dealer noting there was a wide nearly 100-point difference between the day's high and low. Cash price moves also were seen linked to heavy activity in share warrants.
Most-active Novartis registereds continued to decline after recent gains, ending down 10 francs at 2,266.

Roche certificates fluctuated during the session to end 10 francs lower at 13,490. Roche said on Tuesday that its cardiovascular drug known under the trademarked name Posicor has been approved by U.S. authorities.
UBS slid 28 francs, or 1.63 percent, to 1,688. Dealers attributed the drop to technical factors.
In the insurance sector Swiss Re and Zurich Insurance Co posted gains.

One dealer said the market was expecting Zurich to make an announcement soon regarding U.S. asset manager Scudder, Stevens & Clark. Zurich was up four francs at 569, after setting a new year high of 576 francs.
The New York Times reported in May that Zurich was planning to acquire the U.S. money management firm. Zurich has regularly declined to comment on the report.
According to the New York Times, the deal would be worth $1.5 billion.
Nestle added six francs to 1,896. Dealers said the gain was due to technical factors and a new warrant issue on the stock.
On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex), options volume stood at 137,942 contracts.
Dealers said the put ratio in SMI options, and in options on bank shares, was unusually high. The overall call/put ratio was one to 1.24.
On the futures side 4,696 SMI contracts were traded. July SMI futures fell 10.1 points to 5,573.9.
